newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks higher at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were higher at midday Friday, but high techs had lost some ground after a strong start.

The market's early strength gradually concentrated itself in blue chips as some OTC high tech issues turned negative. Stronger-than-forecast earnings from Microsoft Corp boosted the high techs at the opening.
The Dow industrials were up 28 points at 6867, while the Nasdaq Composite Index, a barometer of the high techs, was up five points at 1222 after touching a high of 1232.
Big Board advances led declining issues by about four to three on volume of 216 million shares.

U.S. Treasuries were thinly mixed, with the long bond down 1/32 to yield 7.07 percent. Analysts said the market was feeling some heat from stronger-than-expected consumer confidence data released this morning.
The University of Michigan's preliminary index of consumer sentiment for April rose to 101.0 from a final March reading of 100.0, financial market sources said.
Analysts said the stock market was looking for any sign of moderation in consumer spending and the overall economy.

"I think that macroeconomic factors have stopped influencing the market at this point," said Phil Roth, chief technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds. "Once we get through the quarterly earnings, the market will flip and we'll start worrying about rates and the like again."
He said he felt the market was recovering, despite a minor dip in the Dow industrials Thursday.
"We should expect more recovery. The market is improving," he said. "We could have another test of the lows later in April or in May, but I would advise buying on the dip to exploit the long side."
